items.name: RegexSet
items.summary: Match multiple, possibly overlapping, regexes in a single search.

methods.name: empty
methods.summary: Create a new empty regex set.

methods.name: is_empty
methods.summary: Returns `true` if this set contains no regexes.

methods.name: is_match
methods.summary: Returns true if and only if one of the regexes in this set matches the haystack given.

methods.name: is_match_at
methods.signature: fn is_match_at(&self, haystack: &str, start: usize) -> bool
methods.summary: Returns true if and only if one of the regexes in this set matches the haystack given, with the search starting at the offset given.

methods.name: len
methods.summary: Returns the total number of regexes in this set.

methods.name: matches
methods.summary: Returns the set of regexes that match in the given haystack.

methods.name: matches_at
methods.signature: fn matches_at(&self, haystack: &str, start: usize) -> SetMatches
methods.summary: Returns the set of regexes that match in the given haystack.

methods.name: new
methods.signature: fn new<I, S>(exprs: I) -> Result<RegexSet, Error> where S: AsRef<str>, I: IntoIterator<Item = S>
methods.summary: Create a new regex set with the given regular expressions.

methods.name: patterns
methods.summary: Returns the regex patterns that this regex set was constructed from.

items.name: SetMatches
items.summary: A set of matches returned by a regex set.

methods.name: iter
methods.summary: Returns an iterator over the indices of the regexes that matched.

methods.name: len
methods.summary: The total number of regexes in the set that created these matches.

methods.name: matched
methods.summary: Whether the regex at the given index matched.

methods.name: matched_all
methods.summary: Whether all patterns in this set matched.

methods.name: matched_any
methods.summary: Whether this set contains any matches.

items.name: SetMatchesIntoIter
items.summary: An owned iterator over the set of matches from a regex set.

items.name: SetMatchesIter
items.summary: A borrowed iterator over the set of matches from a regex set.
